scopeNotes: Imported footprints extend to the northern dependencies even in later snapshots. Association is to a geographic history, not certification of that boundary. Saint-Martin and Saint-Barthélemy are explicitly separate from 2007; exact geometry remains unverified.
The Early Ceramic Age range is a broad regional archaeological convention, not a founding date or a claim that all cited sites were occupied throughout it.
La Ramée household clusters and Bisdary-Yuiketi cultivation plots remain interpretations. Calendar dates for those specific structures are not invented.

Leck and colleagues was read in the abstract, table 1 and discussion/conclusion. The identified obsidian source is distinguished from the still-unlocated andesitic glass source; material similarity does not prove a route.
The 1802 order, May fighting and 1848 abolition are separate events. The foundation’s statement about the history of emancipation on other islands is not generalized.
The departmental archives’ opening paragraph contains inconsistent ordinance dates; those dates are omitted. The later register-type descriptions support the public claims.
ANOM’s confused company succession is omitted; its 1635, 1759, 1763 and 1946 chronology is used only as specified.
The UNESCO public description was read in indexed English and French versions. These count as one source, and no independent viewing of the nomination film is claimed.
Literary works are identified through Columbia’s tribute, not represented as books read in full for this packet.
No successor map link is invented. Independent historical review, depth certification and detailed geometry review remain pending.
